title: Check LAPS password complexity
description: Show and configure the complexity settings of the passwords LAPS generates.

windowsCommandTemplate.name: Get-ADObject
windowsCommandTemplate.commandPattern: $domain = Get-ADDomain; Get-GPO -All | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -like '*LAPS*'} | ForEach-Object { Get-GPOReport -Guid $_.Id -ReportType Xml | Select-String -Pattern 'PasswordComplexity|PasswordLength' }

examples.description: List every GPO with 'LAPS' in its name
Check the length of the current LAPS password

Show every property of the first object returned. Select-Object * widens the output to show all columns. -First 1 limits it to the first result. Use this command to discover the available properties before filtering.
Show the results in a table suited to the console. Format-Table -AutoSize fits the column widths for readable output. Ideal to scan structured data quickly.
Export the results to a CSV file usable in Excel. -NoTypeInformation removes the metadata line. -Encoding UTF8 keeps accented characters intact. Useful for archiving, reports and external analysis.
Count the objects returned. Measure-Object returns Count, Sum, Average, Min, Max depending on the properties. Useful for quick statistics and to validate results.

notes: LAPS configuration (through GPO): Length: 12-14 characters minimum recommended (up to 128), Complexity: Enabled (upper case + lower case + digits + symbols), Expiration: 30 days by default. The settings are defined in the GPOs under Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > LAPS.

fr.title: Vérifier la complexité des mots de passe LAPS

fr.notes: Configuration LAPS (via GPO): Longueur: 12-14 caractères minimum recommandé (jusqu'à 128), Complexité: Activée (majuscules + minuscules + chiffres + symboles), Expiration: 30 jours par défaut. Les paramètres sont définis dans les GPO Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > LAPS.
